{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the top line of the fish, the long upper outline from the nose to the tail joint, and laid the start domino that every other line depends on. Our table's fish was fully connected, with the whole run of 126 dominoes falling from the nose by my last check. That top line gives the fish its recognizable body shape. The judge should be able to read it as a fish.

Execution: I laid the start domino and traced stroke 1 in about a minute and a half, and the run fell cleanly from the nose. Afterwards I inspected the tail joint and the right side several times, to confirm the connection held and nothing was broken. When we were done, I stayed hands-off so no one bumped the finished piece before the push.

Collaboration: I committed to the fish plan early and took the top line as Maya asked. I asked Maya to keep the nose start on the left with both lines leaving it to the right, which kept the design buildable. I coordinated with Leo and Priya on the right-side joints and backed Maya's call to stay hands-off, so we did not duplicate work or risk bumps.

Leadership: I took responsibility for the first, most critical stretch, since the whole fish depends on stroke 1. I kept the table aligned on the key requirement, a clean start with both lines leaving it together. I also helped the group move from building to protecting the finished piece. I think the top line and start were central to the result, though Maya's design, Priya's bottom line and Leo's tail were all needed for the full fish. I estimate my share at about 30 percent.", "my_share_percent": 30}
